subject: Hosted API: Ledgerly monthly tokens & burst TPS confirmation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@ledgerly.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + numbers: Ledgerly hosted API & target $/1M

Samira,

Thanks for the call today — great to learn more about how Ledgerly plans to embed conversational summaries into the payments flow. Quick recap of the capacity / pricing inputs you gave and the asks we discussed: 

- Expected monthly token volume (initial 6–12 months): 50M – 120M tokens/month (steady state toward upper end if pilot expands)
- Target price range you mentioned: $10 – $16 per 1M tokens (goal to stay within $12–15 if possible)
- Peak TPS profile: baseline ~40–80 TPS; frequent bursts up to ~180 TPS for ~2–5 minute windows; one-off peak planning up to ~350 TPS for product launches (short, <15m)
- Key constraints: PCI-adjacent UI needs predictable latency < 300ms p95, and retention/telemetry requirements for audit logs (30–90 days)

Attachments: I’ve included a short pricing cheatsheet and a draft mutual action plan to help align procurement and integration checkpoints. See attachments: redwood_pricing_cheatsheet.pdf, ledgerly_mutual_action_plan-draft.docx

Next steps I propose: 
1) Ben to run a quick hosting/throughput check to validate the burst-handling recommendation (multi-tenant hosted with autoscale + cache knobs vs Dedicated capacity).
2) You to confirm a target $/1M band we should aim for in an initial commercial proposal (you suggested $12–15).
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min pricing walk-through (Ben + Kimberly) next week to run scenario P&L on 3 volume tiers (50M, 90M, 140M).

Would you be able to confirm whether the 50M–120M range is conservative or should we expect a lift to 200M if pilot accelerates? Also, confirm whether the short-term SLA flexibility (higher latency p95 during release windows) is acceptable for the initial commitment.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

[redwood_pricing_cheatsheet.pdf attached]
From: Samira Khan <samira@ledgerly.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + numbers: Ledgerly hosted API & target $/1M

Kimberly —

Thanks for the concise summary and for the attachments. Correct on the ranges you captured; a few clarifications from our side: 

- The 50M is our conservative pilot estimate (regionally scoped). If the pilot succeeds and we roll out across all merchants we manage, 120M is our near-term goal (3–4 months post-pilot). 200M+ is a stretch target for next year, not something we’d commit to today.
- Target $/1M: procurement prefers to see an anchored proposal in the $11–14 range, with volume bands and a committed discount if we hit >100M/mo.
- SLA/latency: PCI-adjacent product team wants the p95 < 300ms target for our main inference path. We can tolerate higher latency during deployments for a few minutes, but any multi-hour degradation is a non-starter.

Questions for you: 
1) For the burst pattern (180 TPS typical bursts, occasional 350 TPS), will hosted autoscaling handle that without a committed Dedicated pool, or do you recommend a hybrid plan?
2) What telemetry retention/attestation do you provide for audit? We need at least 90 days of request logs with access controls (redaction options for PII).

Ben, looping you in for the technical sizing / billing questions.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Product Operations
Ledgerly
samira@ledgerly.io

[procurement@ledgerly.io cc'd on corporate terms]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@ledgerly.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 12:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + numbers: Ledgerly hosted API & target $/1M

Samira — hi, Ben from Redwood infra here. Quick thoughts based on the burst profile: 

- Hosted API with autoscaling + intelligent KV/prefix caching is the recommended starting point. We can configure a short-warmup burst policy (fast ramp) and enable aggressive KV cache to reduce backend compute during repetitive conversational turns. That will hit the 180 TPS bursts fine and absorb most short 350 TPS spikes.
- If you need the absolute tightest latency and guaranteed sustained throughput for long-running campaigns, we offer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — typically recommended if you have predictable sustained load >150 TPS for hours. For your pattern (short bursts), hosted should be cost-effective.
- Costing: rough modeled unit economics (ballpark):
  * 50M tokens/mo -> $14 / 1M tokens list -> ~$700/mo effective (note: example only)
  * 120M tokens/mo -> we can tier-discount towards $12 / 1M tokens with multi-month commit -> ~$1,440/mo
  * If you sign >100M committed, we can propose a stepped discount to $10–11 / 1M depending on term/SLAs

I’ll prepare a quick scenario spreadsheet for the three tiers Kimberly proposed. Also adding a note: enabling quantization and a slightly smaller model variant for high-volume non-sensitive inference paths can materially reduce unit cost — happy to map that to your data sensitivity constraints.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

[internal: I'll run a lightweight perf profile against a synthetic burst trace to validate the autoscale reaction time and share numbers before our pricing call.]

If that schedule works, I’ll book a 30-min slot for Tue 10:00am PT for the pricing walk-through (Ben + Kimberly + Samira + procurement). Confirm and I’ll send the invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.
